<content>1: ---
2: title: headers
3: description: API reference for the headers function.
4: ---
5: 
6: `headers` is an **async** function that allows you to **read** the HTTP incoming request headers from a [Server Component](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components).
7: 
8: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
9: import { headers } from 'next/headers'
10: 
11: export default async function Page() {
12:   const headersList = await headers()
13:   const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent')
14: }
15: ```
16: 
17: ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
18: import { headers } from 'next/headers'
19: 
20: export default async function Page() {
21:   const headersList = await headers()
22:   const userAgent = headersList.get('user-agent')
23: }
24: ```
25: 
26: ## Reference
27: 
28: ### Parameters
29: 
30: `headers` does not take any parameters.
31: 
32: ### Returns
33: 
34: `headers` returns a **read-only** [Web Headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers) object.
35: 
36: - [`Headers.entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/entries): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object.
37: - [`Headers.forEach()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/forEach): Executes a provided function once for each key/value pair in this `Headers` object.
38: - [`Headers.get()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/get): Returns a [`String`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String) sequence of all the values of a header within a `Headers` object with a given name.
39: - [`Headers.has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/has): Returns a boolean stating whether a `Headers` object contains a certain header.
40: - [`Headers.keys()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/keys): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object.
41: - [`Headers.values()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/values): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object.
42: 
43: ## Good to know
44: 
45: - `headers` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function.
46:   - In version 14 and earlier, `headers` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
47: - Since `headers` is read-only, you cannot `set` or `delete` the outgoing request headers.
48: - `headers` is a [Dynamic API](/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in will opt a route into **[dynamic rendering](/docs/app/guides/caching#dynamic-rendering)**.
49:

part.text:
I have created a new server component `app/components/user-preferences.tsx` that reads the `theme` cookie and `Accept-Language` header, and integrated it into `app/page.tsx` to display the preferences.

The component uses `cookies()` and `headers()` from `next/headers` to access the request data on the server. If the `theme` cookie is missing, it defaults to "light".
